A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ESAM work. All pages, equations, tables and figures were readable, including v2's Appendix A.1–A.6. Relocated material can be matched reliably; v1 has no separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation, dataset-transfer, data-efficiency and ablation results, including ESAM results in Tables 1–8.

after.justification: v2 reports original results throughout Section 4 and the appendix, including revised benchmark scores and new pooling-weight and cross-dataset visualizations.

M1.justification: The query lifting, dual-level decoder, auxiliary tasks, online merging and losses remain unchanged in Section 3 and Equations 1–9. Section 4.1 newly documents superpoint-level mask prediction for the first two iterations before point-level prediction, but presents this as implementation detail rather than establishing a newly introduced algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions cover ScanNet, ScanNet200, SceneNN and 3RScan, retaining class-agnostic, standard instance, transfer and open-vocabulary evaluations. The added ScanNet class-agnostic table uses already represented scenes and task requirements. Open-vocabulary evaluation is retained in Appendix A.4, not removed.

E2.justification: v2 adds the 2D version of Open3DIS with GroundedSAM to Tables 1–2 and the appendix comparison. HDBSCAN, Nunes et al., Felzenszwalb et al. and UnScene3D disappear from the ScanNet200 comparison, although they appear in v2's ScanNet Table 7. The standard instance-segmentation and open-vocabulary comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Architecture and merging ablations are reported on ScanNet(-25k) in v2 instead of ScanNet200(-25k) in v1. The data-efficiency table replaces the 20% training condition with 10%, although v2's introductory sentence still says 20%. Main dataset splits, AP metrics and eight-frame training sampling remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.5/Figure 7 adds inspection of geometric-aware pooling weights, and A.6/Figure 8 adds qualitative error comparisons on SceneNN and 3RScan. Existing architecture, merging and data-efficiency analyses remain, with revised settings and results. The inference-time decomposition and online visualization are relocated rather than newly added analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Revised point estimates do not change the uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 substantially revise reported scores. ScanNet200 AP changes from 37.9 to 42.2 for ESAM and from 35.9 to 43.4 for ESAM-E, reversing their ranking. SAI3D's 3RScan AP changes from 5.4 to 8.1. v2 also adds ScanNet class-agnostic results and replaces ablation/data-efficiency entries; changed ablation settings prevent direct performance comparisons. Open-vocabulary scores and timing decomposition remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions and Equations 1–9 are retained. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs, and v2's curriculum-learning explanation introduces no formal derivation.

C1.justification: v2 removes open-vocabulary segmentation from the headline contributions in the abstract, introduction and conclusion, while retaining its experiment in Appendix A.4. The central online, real-time and generalization claims remain; the abstract more explicitly scopes its offline comparison to VFM-assisted methods.

C2.justification: v2 interprets pooling weights as suppressing noisy boundaries and emphasizing objects, especially small ones, and describes early superpoint predictions as curriculum learning. Its 3RScan discussion replaces the specific SAI3D-versus-SAM3D explanation with a broader discussion of offline methods. Existing runtime limitations remain, with pruning and distillation added as possible future remedies.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies the decoder's first-two-iteration superpoint prediction schedule. Conversely, v2 removes v1's project hyperlink and single-RTX-3090 training/evaluation statement, replacing available code and demo with a future-release statement. These are changes in disclosed implementation and access information, not evidence that resource availability was externally verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Open3DIS, GroundedSAM, OpenIns3D, LangSplat, Gaussian Grouping, pruning and distillation, while dropping GNFactor. Related work gains a brief discussion of Gaussian scene representations. The central positioning around learnable, online lifting and merging remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The five main sections and most method prose are retained. v2 edits the abstract and conclusion, adds a compared-methods paragraph, changes citation style and publication headers, and organizes relocated and additional material into six appendix subsections. This is a limited narrative revision rather than an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the visual presentation: it adds pooling-weight and cross-dataset figures plus a separate ScanNet benchmark table, and moves the online visualization, timing table and open-vocabulary table into the appendix. Tables are restructured, existing visualizations are updated, and the ICLR format changes typography, headers and figure/table placement throughout.

improvement.justification: Open3DIS comparisons and the new pooling and transfer visualizations strengthen empirical scrutiny. However, v2 removes useful access/hardware information and introduces reporting inconsistencies: Figure 1 retains a 15.7-point gap despite displaying 43.4 versus 20.2 AP, and the 10%-data state-of-the-art claim conflicts with ESAM's 32.8 AP versus Open3DIS's 34.6. These gains and losses leave the net direction of overall quality uncertain.
